images.title: Nebraska and Kansas territories map (Colton, 1855)

images.note: Anti-slavery cartoon, 1856 (contemporary; LC-USZ62-92023): Kansas personified as the bound 'fair maid' Liberty assaulted by Border Ruffians. Serves the 1855 election-fraud beat and the self-test Q2 ballot-box cartoon stimulus.
images.title: 'Liberty, the fair maid of Kansas' in the hands of the Border Ruffians (1856 cartoon)

images.note: Anti-slavery cartoon, 1856 (contemporary; LC-USZ62-92043). Visualizes the popular-sovereignty mechanism the script attacks: slavery forced on the territories. TIFF master.
images.title: 'Forcing slavery down the throat of a freesoiler' (1856 cartoon)

images.alt_source: World History Encyclopedia (State Historical Society of Missouri)
images.note: Ruins of the Free State Hotel (Emigrant Aid Company HQ), Lawrence, after the May 21, 1856 sack (contemporary; LC-USZ62-53868). Kansas Historical Society holds other contemporary views but their portal blocked automated verification from this environment.
images.title: Ruins of the Free State Hotel, Lawrence, after the 1856 sack

images.note: Earliest known likeness of John Brown: quarter-plate daguerreotype by African American abolitionist Augustus Washington, c.1846-47 (contemporary; NPG.96.123). Pre-dates Kansas; honest contemporary portrait for the Pottawatomie beat. Other copies (Kansas Historical Society, Nelson-Atkins) not verifiable at >=1200px from this environment.
images.title: John Brown, daguerreotype (Augustus Washington, c.1846-47)

images.note: Franklin Pierce, oil by G.P.A. Healy, November 1852 (contemporary; NPG). The president who recognized the pro-slavery Lecompton government and called the Topeka government traitorous.
images.title: Franklin Pierce, portrait (G.P.A. Healy, 1852)

images.note: Charles Sumner, oil by William Morris Hunt, 1875 — LATER portrait (posthumous; Sumner died 1874). No contemporary Sumner photograph verified at >=1200px (LOC Brady-Handy service files cap at ~1024px; NPG catalog blocked automated access). Use with 'later portrait' caption honesty.
images.title: Charles Sumner, portrait (William Morris Hunt, 1875)

images.alt_source: Smarthistory (holding institution: Library Company of Philadelphia)
images.note: John L. Magee, 'Southern chivalry — argument versus club's,' 1856 (contemporary; LC-USZ62-38851): Brooks beating Sumner at his Senate desk, Sumner clutching the 'Kansas' speech. images.note: 'Col. John C. Fremont, Republican candidate for President of the United States,' campaign print, c.1856 (contemporary; LC-USZ62-91388) — carries the script's 1856 Republican beat and slogan context. ALT: Ball, Black & Co. photograph of Fremont, 1856 (contemporary).
